question.worked_solution:
Recall that if ${X}_{1},{X}_{2},…,{X}_{n}$ are independent and identically distributed (I.I.D) normal random variables, where 

$$
{X}_{i}∼N(\mu ,{\sigma }^{2}),\,1\le i\le n,
$$

then 

$$
Y={X}_{1}+{X}_{2}+⋯+{X}_{n}∼N(n\mu ,\,n{\sigma }^{2}).
$$

Therefore, since ${X}_{1},{X}_{2},…,{X}_{100}$ are independent and identically distributed, we have 

$$
\begin{aligned}Y={X}_{1}+{X}_{2}+⋯+{X}_{100} & ∼N(100\cdot (-0.05),\,100\cdot {0.1}^{2}) \\  & ∼N(100\cdot (-0.05),\,100\cdot 0.01) \\  & =N(-5,1).\end{aligned}
$$

We wish to compute the probability $P(Y\ge -4.25).$ We first convert $Y$ into a standard normal random variable by $z$-scoring:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(Y\ge -4.25) & =P(Z\ge \frac{-4.25-(-5)}{\sqrt{1}}) \\  & =P(Z\ge 0.75) \\  & =1-P(Z\le 0.75) \\  & =1-Φ(0.75)\end{aligned}
$$

From the $z$-table, we have

$$
Φ(0.75)=0.7734.
$$

Therefore,

$$
P(Y\ge -4.25)=1-Φ(0.75)=0.2266.
$$
